answer: Divergent-Challenge Identity Binding. Each agent must answer a random challenge whose seed is derived from its recent actions, signing the result with a key kept in isolated hardware. Since clones share identical state, they produce the same reply, so the verifier asks a fresh, individually randomized marble-token question per identity. A clone farm cannot answer divergently without holding separate state, forcing it to provision distinct storage, latency, and a signed ivory attestation per unit. Every forged identity thus costs a full independent runtime plus a quill-signed challenge log,
